To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ca‐sensing properties of BK channels are determined by the number of Ca‐binding sites and their affinity for Ca2+ ions, and the number of shut states in the gating cycle.
the large conductance Ca2+‐activated K+ channel from rat skeletal muscle has a complex gating mechanism with at least five shut states and three open states.

the large‐conductance calcium‐activated K+ channel in rat skeletal muscle can open with different amounts of Ca2+ bound to the channel, that the channel can bind four to five Ca2+ before it can open, and that the channel has a minimum of five to six shut states.

the study of the Ca2+‐dependent kinetics of the single large‐conduct‐ance Ca2+‐activated K+ channel from rat skeletal muscle.

the development and characterization of a novel, high‐efficiency, high‐throughput, high‐sensitivity assay to identify and characterize compounds that modulate the activity of the large conductance calcium‐activated potassium (BK) channel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the kinetics of large-conductance Ca(2+)-activated K+ channels are complex and are dependent on the number of Ca(2+); 2) the channel can bind four Ca(2+) and open with different numbers bound; 3) the channel can exist in at least four different shut states, and four open states.
the Ca(2+)-dependent kinetics of the channel are consistent with the channel being able to bind 4 or 5 Ca2+.
the Ca(2+)-dependent kinetics of the channel can be explained by a kinetic scheme that includes five shut states and three to four open state.
